name: Isshiah
overview: Isshiah was a male Levite known as a descendant of Uzziel, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 23:20. His genealogy places him within the tribe of Levi, which was set apart for priestly and temple duties. Beyond his lineage, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or notes about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Isshiah means "y-h-v-h forgets," reflecting a Hebrew theophoric element referencing the LORD. This proper name, found in 1 Chronicles 23:20, is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful connection to divine remembrance or forgetfulness.
familyAndRelationships: Isshiah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Uzziel, a notable Levite ancestor. It is also inferred that Zechariah was his father, based on 1 Chronicles 24:25, though this is not explicitly stated. Scripture does not record further family relationships beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Isshiah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the Levitical line descending from Uzziel, which situates him in the context of the priestly divisions responsible for temple service. This lineage underscores the continuity of God's appointed servants in Israel and reflects the orderly organization of Levitical families for sacred duties. Although not prominent in narrative events, his mention preserves the heritage and identity of the Levites during the time chronicled.
